images.title: Hops of one seventh
images.purpose: Show 4/7 + 6/7 as six hops of 1/7 from the 4/7 mark, landing on 10/7.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the middle with wide margins, with hop arcs above it.
images.exact_structure: One straight horizontal number line from 0 to 2 in grey #6B7280 with 15 evenly spaced tick marks, 14 equal gaps of 1/7; taller ticks at 0, 1 and 2. One teal #0072B2 dot on the 5th tick, at 4/7. Six equal amber #E69F00 arcs above the line, each spanning exactly one gap, from 4/7 to 10/7. One reddish purple #CC79A7 ring on the 11th tick, at 10/7. Exactly 1 line, 15 ticks, 1 dot, 6 arcs, 1 ring.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
ticks that are not evenly spaced, or arcs of different widths
images.takeaway: Start at the first fraction and hop the second in unit gaps.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 2 in sevenths: starting at 4/7, six hops of 1/7 pass 1 and land on 10/7 = 1 3/7.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the arcs, not the ticks, from 4/7 and say where the sixth hop lands.

image_decisions.why: Hops on a number line give a second view of the same sum; one picture shows it.
